description:
fz has two answers to "which module does this name mean":
- resolve_module_name (src/compiler2/world.rs:2410) falls back to reference_module, so a name means the module of that name, as in Elixir. Types and other references use it.
- lookup_module_path (world.rs:2449) has no fallback. callable_name_qualifier (world.rs:2073) uses it for a qualified callee, so `Enum.count(x)` resolves only because the prelude binds `alias Enum` (lib/runtime.fz:4-17). Deleting those aliases turned 153 lib tests red with "unresolved direct runtime callee Enum.count/1" (probe recorded in the fz-sc8.4 run).

Fold: one resolution. Qualified callees resolve through the same authority as every other module name, and the 15 single-segment identity aliases in the prelude are deleted in the same change (keep `alias String.Chars`, which binds the short name Chars).

Before building, confirm that a call to a module that exists nowhere still fails loudly (an unknown module/function diagnostic), rather than resolving quietly to an empty id. callable_name_qualifier has no owning module today, while resolve_module_name takes current_module; the page settles how the owner is threaded.

Blocks fz-sc8.3, which touches the same callee qualifier for atom modules (:erlang.f).
title: A qualified call finds its module the way every other name does
